blocks.x: Blockchain & Digital Trust applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Banking & Financial Services, blockchain & digital trust delivers distributed-ledger programs where a shared, verifiable record has economic value: enterprise dlt networks for multi-party workflows, asset tokenization, smart contract engineering and audit, provenance and traceability, decentralized identity with verifiable credentials, and on-chain analytics for compliance. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: enterprise dlt network engineering, asset tokenization & digital assets, smart contract engineering & audit — delivered on Dataq Ledger and Dataq Sentinel with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: T+2/T+1 cycles, multi-party reconciliation and dispute evidence spread across counterparties consume operations capacity. Interbank workflows still reconcile by exchanging files and hoping.

Customer due diligence refresh cycles lag behind actual risk changes; files queue for weeks in review pools while remediation backlogs grow. Manual file assembly across registries, screening tools and core systems consumes analyst hours that produce no judgment.
GenAI stuck between pilot and policy

Generative assistants for credit memos, research summaries and client drafts stall in model-risk review because guardrails, provenance and audit trails were not designed in. Shadow AI fills the gap, creating exactly the exposure the review was meant to prevent.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 6 services from the Blockchain & Digital Trust tower — Enterprise DLT Network Engineering, Asset Tokenization & Digital Assets, Smart Contract Engineering & Audit, Provenance, Traceability & Supply Chain Trust as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: DORA (EU) obligations shape the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Permissioned networks for multi-party truth: governance, consensus and integration done institutionally.
Instruments as tokens: issuance, custody and lifecycle under securities-law discipline.
Contracts as production software: specification, formal verification and audit before value moves.
Proof, not paperwork: EUDR, DPP and chain-of-custody systems regulators and customers can verify.
Permissioned DLT with shared custody-event evidence replacing file exchange (reconciliation effort down 70%)
Permissioned issuance with transfer controls and custody integration under securities discipline (collateral mobilization cycle compressed)
From weeks to days with agentic assembly and review

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: DORA (EU) and PSD2 / PSD3 and instant payments. Real-time rails with fraud and SCA obligations. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
